title: Progressive Degradation Controller for Regional SLO Protection
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: During partial region outages and bursty traffic we have seen cascading probe noise that triggers autoscaler churn and blunt, multi-region failovers that violate 99th percentile latency and availability SLOs. Current readiness/liveness probing is too binary and reacts to short-lived tail events, which leads to premature circuit trips and aggressive global failovers.

Goal: Implement a Progressive Degradation Controller (PDC) that smooths health signals, applies request-priority-aware shedding, and orchestrates region-level circuit breakers with graded degradation tiers to preserve customer-facing SLOs while avoiding unnecessary autoscaler oscillation. The controller should integrate with existing readiness probes, synthetic transaction runners, and the autoscaler decision pipeline.

Success criteria / deliverables:
- Design doc outlining degradation tiers, scoring model for regional health, and interaction contract with autoscaler (see attachments).
- Implementation of a PDC service + runtime hooks that: (1) ingests probe and synthetic transaction metrics, (2) computes a region health score with hysteresis, (3) exposes a graded readiness signal (OK / Degraded / Critical) to the autoscaler and routing plane, (4) emits shedding directives (percent-based request drop by priority class).
- E2E simulation harness and load-tests that demonstrate preserved p99 latency and >99.9% availability for critical-tier customers under two failure modes: (a) slow-starting kernel upgrades, (b) cross-region network blips.
- Dashboard and alerting: per-region health score, shedding rate, autoscaler state transitions, and rollback knobs.

Non-goals: This ticket does not include tenant billing changes for shed requests or a universal policy editor UI. Integration scope is limited to the serving runtime and control-plane APIs for Dedicated and Hosted for now.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Region health score documented and computed deterministically from probe+synthetic inputs; 2) Graded readiness signal consumed by autoscaler simulation and production rollout (canary) without causing sequential scale-to-zero cycles; 3) Default shedding policy protects critical priority traffic until region recovers or fallback satisfies SLO; 4) Performance overhead of PDC < 2% p50 latency on control-plane calls; 5) Observability shows reduced autoscaler churn in canary run vs baseline.
comments: 2026-02-20 - Aisha P. - Triage: Flagged as P1 because customer-impact for mid-market + dedicated customers observed in recent incident (INC-2026-119). Assigned to Marco for implementation planning.

2026-02-25 - Marco L. - Design spike: Completed prototype scoring model (exponential moving average of p50/p95/p99 combined with synthetic tx timeouts). Draft design uploaded to Confluence (link below). Need PM input on priority classes mapping to shedding percentages.

2026-03-01 - Priya Menon (PM) - Feedback: Agree with 3-tier degradation (OK/Degraded/Critical). Requested that critical-tier customers (SLA-backed) are never shed below 95% of baseline throughput unless region is declared Critical. Added parent issue PM-8893 for product gating decisions.

2026-03-04 - Marco L. - Implementation update: Completed POC that emits graded readiness via existing readiness API as a new header X-Region-Readiness: OK|DEGRADED|CRITICAL. Hooked into autoscaler simulation harness. Observed 40% reduction in autoscaler up/down events in short-duration bursts during local tests.

2026-03-09 - Eng review: Martin Gomez and Elena R. reviewed the POC. Comments: need to replace simple EMA with an outlier-resistant aggregation (trimmed-mean + quantile gating) and add explicit cooldown windows to avoid flip-flopping during rolling deploys. Action: swap aggregation and add cooldown config flags.

2026-03-11 - Load test: Ran 120-minute blast with interleaved network partition sim. Baseline p99 increased by 18% in control; with PDC enabled p99 stayed within SLO for critical traffic and improved overall availability. Attachments include raw results and Grafana snapshots.

2026-03-12 - Next steps: Finalize aggregation algorithm, add priority-queue-aware shedding in runtime, open PR for control-plane API changes, schedule canary in eu-west-1 with 10% traffic, create runbook for rollback and postmortem triggers.
